approach_variants.name: Round Mountain Trail #1529 to Nason Ridge and the lookout spur
approach_variants.notes: From the highway just past the rest area, turn north onto the unsigned Butcher Creek Road (Forest Road 6910) — the turn is on a curve with fast traffic, so watch for it — and follow good gravel a few miles before turning onto the short spur that ends at the Round Mountain Trailhead. Round Mountain Trail #1529 climbs steeply for about a mile and a half through forest and an older burn to its junction with Nason Ridge Trail #1583. Turn left and west and follow the ridge trail, which undulates along the crest for a few miles to the lookout spur. A longer alternative reaches the same ridge trail from the west via the Merritt Lake trail, used mainly for through-hikes or when this side is inaccessible.
approach_variants.season: Roughly July through October once the ridge melts out; the lookout is one of the few in the range still staffed.
hazards: The turn off the highway is on a blind curve with fast traffic
The ridge trail narrows to a knife edge with steep rock-filled gullies dropping away on both sides
The crest is exposed to weather with no shelter along it
The lower trail climbs steeply through burn with little shade or water
approach_variants.baseFinding: A '9' nailed to a tree is the marker, and the knife edge is the confirmation. Walking west along Nason Ridge Trail #1583, the crest pinches down to a ten-foot-wide knife edge with steep, rock-filled gullies falling away to the highway on the south and into the river drainage on the north — that narrowing is Ninemile Saddle, and a sign carrying the numeral 9 is fixed to a tree there. It is the only labelled feature on this stretch of ridge. From the saddle the lookout spur breaks right and climbs the last short distance to the staffed lookout on the summit. The negative marker is simple: the ridge trail carries straight on west past the spur, so if the ground has stopped climbing, the crest has widened out again, and no building has come into view, you have walked through the junction and should turn back to the narrow section with the numbered tree.
